description: Four-panel composite of optical micrographs (OM), all grayscale, each with a black 20 µm scale bar in the lower-right corner and a panel label (a)–(d) in the upper-left. Panels are as-cast Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C-xCr low-density strips: (a) 0Cr, (b) 3Cr, (c) 6Cr, (d) 9Cr. In every panel the austenite matrix appears as the light continuous phase and δ-ferrite as darker, outlined second-phase particles; no other phase is clearly resolved. (a) shows sparse, small, rod-like to short-elongated ferrite particles, several loosely grouped near grain centres. (b) and (c) show progressively larger, more angular and more block-like particles with dendritic outlines, locally aligned in rows. (d) shows the densest population of blocky, partly interconnected ferrite. The four panels make one argument: increasing Cr both raises the ferrite fraction and changes ferrite morphology from rod-like to block-like while ferrite stays dispersed in the austenite matrix. No numbers other than the 20 µm scale bars are printed on any panel.

observations.observation: The group consists of four grayscale optical micrographs arranged as a 2×2 composite, labelled (a)–(d) top-left, each with a 20 µm black scale bar at bottom-right.
In all four panels the continuous light-grey phase (austenite matrix) surrounds darker, delineated second-phase particles (ferrite); no additional phase is visually distinguishable.
Panel (a) (0Cr) contains the fewest and finest ferrite particles, with a rod-like/short-elongated shape, whereas panels (b)–(d) show progressively larger and blockier particles.
Panel (d) (9Cr) shows the highest areal density of ferrite and the most interconnection/linking between neighbouring block-like particles.
The ferrite particles in (b) and (d) tend to be arranged in row-like/curved bands rather than uniformly at random, consistent with alignment along solidification cell or grain boundaries.
The caption states the panels are OM of as-cast Fe–28Mn–9Al-1.2C-xCr low-density strips with (a) 0Cr, (b) 3Cr, (c) 6Cr, (d) 9Cr.

The citing text reports ferrite volume fractions of 10.2 vol% (0Cr), 11.4 vol% (3Cr), 14.8 vol% (6Cr) and 19.6 vol% (9Cr), measured quantitatively with Gatan Digital Micrograph; these numbers are not printed on the images.
The citing text states that ferrite is uniformly distributed in the austenite matrix and that Cr addition changes ferrite shape from rod-like to block-like gradually.
The citing text states that in Fig. 2(a) all ferrites lie at the centres of austenite grains, indicating that δ-ferrite first nucleated and grew from the melt during near-rapid solidification.
The citing text attributes the microstructure to the FA solidification mode: L → L+δ → L+δ+γ → δ+γ.
Fine dark speckles visible in panels (c) and (d) are not identified by any label in the figure; their nature (pores, inclusions or etch pits) cannot be determined from the images.

subfigures.description: Optical micrograph of as-cast 0Cr strip with 20 µm scale bar. Small, rod-like/short-elongated dark ferrite particles dispersed sparsely in a light austenite matrix, several particles clustered toward grain interiors.

Optical micrograph of as-cast 3Cr strip with 20 µm scale bar. Larger, more abundant, partly block-like and dendritic-outlined ferrite particles, locally aligned in rows within the light austenite matrix.
Optical micrograph of as-cast 6Cr strip with 20 µm scale bar. Predominantly angular/block-like ferrite particles, more numerous and coarser than in (b), dispersed in the light matrix.
Optical micrograph of as-cast 9Cr strip with 20 µm scale bar. Highest density of block-like ferrite; some particles are linked/interconnected, forming irregular networks in the austenite matrix.
